details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has launched a new service that connects its payment system to blockchain-based financial markets, signaling a broader effort by central banks to adapt to and leverage blockchain technology. The ECB also indicated it would invest some of its own funds in digital securities. This move aligns with statements from ECB board member Isabel Schnabel, who last month advocated for central banks to "go on-chain" to reduce reliance on private alternatives, a trend also seen with initiatives from the Swiss National Bank and the Bank of England.
title: ECB Integrates Blockchain into Financial Markets

details: Mike McGlone, a senior commodity strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, has issued a warning that the cryptocurrency market faces a challenging outlook. He suggests a "lose-lose" scenario due to persistent poor returns and extreme volatility since 2017. McGlone attributes this to a hawkish Federal Reserve, which diminishes market liquidity, and the high correlation of crypto assets with an overvalued S&P 500. This environment, he argues, creates significant headwinds for highly volatile digital assets.
title: Bloomberg Analyst Warns Crypto Faces "Lose-Lose" Amid Hawkish Fed, Stock Correlation

details: Bitcoin surged past the $84,000 mark, achieving its highest price this month, fueled by a combination of factors. A fourth consecutive session of declining international oil prices contributed to a renewed "risk-on" sentiment in financial markets. This, coupled with significant net inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), sparked broad buying across risk assets, including cryptocurrencies and equities. The resolution of macroeconomic uncertainty following the recent Federal Reserve meeting also supported a relief rally.
title: Bitcoin Rallies Past $84,000 on Retreating Oil Prices, Strong ETF Inflows

details: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde reportedly played a key role in preventing the cryptocurrency exchange Binance from securing an EU license under the new MiCA regulations. The intervention was reportedly driven by concerns over Binance's substantial holdings of dollar-pegged stablecoins, estimated to be around $300 billion. This development highlights increased scrutiny from central banking authorities on large stablecoin operations within the European Union and suggests a tightening regulatory stance.
title: ECB Chief Lagarde Reportedly Sank Binance's EU Bid Over Stablecoin Concerns

details: The proposed Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed to pass in the U.S. Senate, a significant setback for the cryptocurrency industry. This legislative failure is expected to prolong and potentially intensify the ongoing "turf war" between the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) regarding oversight of digital assets. The lack of clear, comprehensive federal regulation continues to create uncertainty for crypto businesses and investors in the United States.
title: US Digital Asset Market Clarity Act Fails, Sparks Regulatory Uncertainty

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its target interest rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75%-4% on September 16, citing elevated inflation as the primary reason. This marks the first rate hike since July 2023. While typically a move that could pressure risk assets, Bitcoin initially showed a limited reaction to the announcement, hovering near $76,000-$80,000. Markets had largely anticipated the hike, suggesting it was mostly priced in. However, the sustained tighter monetary policy backdrop from the Fed remains a critical macroeconomic factor for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, moving forward.
title: Fed Hikes Interest Rates to 3.75%-4%, Bitcoin Shows Limited Reaction
